RFK Jr. is tackling the real issue: decades of bureaucratic bloat at agencies like CDC that prioritize pet projects over frontline results. The HIV prevention division’s $500k per patient cost proves systemic failure—throwing more money at broken systems isn’t compassion, it’s negligence. While Congress clings to legacy programs, the administration’s focus is cutting red tape to deliver care directly to Americans without middlemen skimming billions.

The 12% HIV reduction since 2018? Achieved despite—not because of—DC’s bloated bureaucracy. Real progress happens when we bypass gatekeepers and fund medical innovation free from Pharma capture. Redirecting resources to border health security and streamlined prevention models will protect communities better than maintaining failed programs designed to self-perpetuate.

Accountability matters: every dollar spent on HIV should show measurable outcomes, not disappear into agency slush funds. If existing structures can’t prove efficiency, they deserve scrutiny. The administration’s reforms aim to rescue public health from career bureaucrats who’ve turned critical services into lifetime employment programs. Americans deserve transparency, not fearmongering from politicians protecting their pork.
